subject: Urgent: Transatlantic route shift causing p95/p99 surge for MedTech AI
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@medtech.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Latency spike - hosted API impacting inference p95/p99

Stephanie —

We started seeing a large jump in p95 and p99 around 07:30 UTC this morning. Our synthetic tests show p95 went from ~120ms to ~480ms and p99 to ~1.2s. Error rate also ticked up briefly. This is affecting our overnight batch scoring jobs and a couple of real-time routes.

I pulled a trace from our app and attached the short traceroute — it looks like traffic from our EU region is being routed to a US egress for several hops. Can you confirm routing changes on your side? Our dashboards: https://dash.medtech.ai/inference/alerts/7621

We need this mitigated ASAP; can we get an ETA and rollback if necessary? Also, if you expect any customer credit related to this, let us know.

Thanks,
Amit
Ops Lead, MedTech AI
(ops@medtech.ai)

Attachment: traceroute_medtech_0830.txt
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@medtech.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:30:00 +01:00
Subject: Fwd: Latency spike - hosted API impacting inference p95/p99

Hey Marcus / Neha — forwarding an urgent customer report from MedTech AI. They see a sharp p95/p99 regression starting ~07:30 UTC and suspect EU->US egress on the path (traceroute attached).

Quick summary:
- Impact: synthetic p95 ~480ms, p99 ~1.2s for EU region routes; brief error rate increase
- Scope: reported by MedTech; we see correlated RT increases in the EU-hosted API dashboard (spike at 07:28–07:45 UTC)
- Customer: enterprise (MedTech AI), on Dedicated+Hosted integration; account flagged as high-touch

Ask: Marcus — can you validate routing tables and recent infra pushes that could cause cross-region pathing? Neha — please coordinate comms and temporary mitigations for the customer. This needs exec attention if we can't get a quick rollback.

I've included Amit from the customer for transparency.

-Steph

Signature: Stephanie Nguyen
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@medtech.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 10:05:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency spike - hosted API impacting inference p95/p99

Thanks — I pulled the routing and load reports. Early findings: we had a control-plane rollout that adjusted egress mapping for a small subset of EU availability zones at 07:15 UTC as part of a peering optimization. It looks like one rollout bucket had an incorrect AS-path preference that favored the transatlantic peer.

Evidence attached: traceroute_medtech_0830.txt (customer), and internal traceroutes showing hop shifts. Sample log excerpt: 

[08:28:22] route-map apply: az-eu-west-2a -> prefer-peer-us-1 (config-id: rmg-7b9)
[08:28:22] detected path length increase: +4 hops for flow dst=medtech-ai-eu
[08:29:05] telemetry: p95_inference_eu spike -> 460ms

Action I'm taking now:
- Immediately halt the rollout on the bucket (done: 10:02 UTC)
- Trigger control-plane rollback to previous egress preference (initiated 10:04 UTC)
- Spin up a temporary regional capacity pad to absorb in-flight requests for medtech-ai EU routes (ETA 15 mins)

I'll follow up with confirmation of rollback completion and a mitigation timeline. If rollback doesn't reduce p95 within the next 30m, we'll initiate a route pin for the customer's sessions to a stable border peer.

-Marcus

Attachment: internal_traceroute_sample_0830.txt
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@medtech.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 10:20:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike - hosted API impacting inference p95/p99

Hi Amit — thanks for the quick signal and traceroute. We’re on it. Marcus has initiated a rollback of the recent egress mapping change and we’ve temporarily pinned a stable EU border peer for your account to avoid transatlantic egress while we validate.

Planned timeline: 
- 10:05 UTC: rollback initiated (control-plane)
- 10:20 UTC: temporary peer pin applied for MedTech AI
- 10:35 UTC: observe metric reduction window (p95/p99 expected to trend down)

We’ll keep you updated every 15 minutes. If you see anything else from your side, please send the traces. We’ll also provide a formal incident note and post-mortem once resolved.

Thanks for patience — sorry for the disruption.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Attachment: p95_snapshot_0830.png
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@medtech.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 14:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Resolved: Transatlantic route shift — MedTech AI impact and next steps

Amit — following up with final status and next steps.

Summary: 
- Root cause: misapplied egress preference in a control-plane rollout caused a subset of EU flows to prefer a US transatlantic peer, increasing RTT and causing the observed p95/p99 regressions.
- Mitigation: rollback completed and temporary peer pin applied; regional capacity pad held steady during validation.
- Outcome: By 10:40 UTC on 2026-08-30 p95 returned to baseline (~125ms) and p99 back within SLA. Error spikes subsided.

Customer impact remediation: 
- We’re issuing a one-month service credit for the window of degraded performance (details / credit amount will be formalized by finance).
- Post-mortem and corrective actions: control-plane rollout validation tightened, additional canary checks for egress path shifts added, and a runbook for immediate peer-pinning for high-touch customers.

Next steps (owner):
- Marcus: follow-up Jira OPS-4821 with RCA and config patch (ETA 2026-09-03)
- Neha: share post-incident note and coordinate credit with Finance/CS (ETA 2026-09-02)
- Stephanie: schedule executive brief and account outreach call with MedTech (ETA 2026-09-01)

Thanks again for flagging this so quickly — we appreciate your partnership and are committed to preventing recurrence.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
